questions.text: In a music generator that autoregressively predicts neural-codec tokens, what converts the generated token sequence into an audible waveform?
questions.explanation: The language model predicts discrete audio-codec tokens, and the codec decoder reconstructs waveform samples from those tokens.

questions.text: Generated music has a low FAD relative to a reference set but often ignores the text prompt. Which additional evaluation directly targets prompt adherence?

options.B: Compare generated and reference file sizes.

questions.explanation: FAD compares audio embedding distributions; CLAP compares the text prompt with the generated audio to assess alignment.

questions.text: The toy tempo parser starts with bpm = 120. For each whitespace-separated token ending in "bpm", it tries int(token[:-3]) and ignores ValueError. What bpm results from the prompt "pop at 140 bpm"?
questions.explanation: The token "140" does not end in "bpm"; the token "bpm" yields int("") and a caught ValueError. The initial 120 remains.
